root_idea.summary: Classical evidence records three distinct, non-analogical branches for this root: testing or trial, giving or withholding, and striking with a whip.
root_idea.development: The Quranic Form VIII verb develops the testing-and-trial branch, alongside the related noun مِحْنَةٌ. The reported giving and striking branches remain separate Classical Arabic usages rather than extensions of the Quranic verb's sense.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form VIII verb with an independently supported testing/trial meaning.

senses.definition: To test, examine, or put through trial.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of testing people or hearts. The Quranic usages include examining persons and describing hearts as tested in relation to piety; these are applications of the same testing or trial construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trial, ordeal, or afflicting test.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in a negative construction meaning, “I came to him, but he gave me nothing.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike someone with a whip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction specifying the whip as the instrument.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Defines مِحْنَةٌ as a trial or afflicting ordeal.
Pointer and orthographic correction directing the reader elsewhere; it supplies no lexical definition for this root.

cautions: The Classical record explicitly treats testing, giving, and striking as separate non-analogical branches; the latter two should not be inferred as meanings of the Quranic Form VIII verb.
